head: claude/send-ping-kind-params
title: send-ping: make the three ping classes reachable from the action
body:
## Summary

`src/runtime/claude_ping.py` defines three ping CLASSES — `decision`, `state_change`, `lifecycle` — with deliberately different gating, and `scripts/send_ping.py` has accepted `--kind`/`--why`/`--unproven` since #10669. But **`scripts/ops/send_ping_action.sh` passed none of them**, so the `send-ping` system-action could only ever fire the passthrough shape.

⚠️ **So the classes were implemented, documented, and unreachable from the only path a session can dispatch.** That is the same family as #10674 — a capability that is configured, resolvable and inert — and it is why the three classes could not be exercised end to end against the live bot without this.

## ⚠️ Passthrough stays the DEFAULT, and that is the design decision

A blank `kind` carries the **operator's own text, unaltered**. Format B is a house style for MACHINE-generated events; forcing a human sentence into "headline / why" would rewrite what someone chose to say. So this is not a migration and passthrough is not a legacy mode — it is the primary path, and every branch added below is a no-op when `kind` is empty.

The no-kind invocation is pinned in the tests as an **exact argv list**, not a subset — a stray `--kind ''` would still satisfy "contains `--target`", and a silent extra flag reshaping an operator's words is precisely the failure being prevented.

## An invalid `kind` is a HARD ERROR, never a fallback to passthrough

Deliberately **unlike** the neighbouring `priority`/`target` cases, which warn and default. Those pick a prefix or a destination, and a wrong one is visible in the delivered message. `kind` selects the **format and the rate limiter**, so silently degrading a misspelled `state-change` to passthrough would send an unformatted ping, record nothing against the limiter, and report success — the caller who asked for a gated, formatted ping would have no way to tell they did not get one.

The same reasoning refuses `why:`/`unproven:` **without** a `kind:`: the producer only reads them on the Format-B path, so they would otherwise be accepted and silently discarded while the caller believed they had attached a second line.

## A withheld ping is not a sent ping

`send_ping.py` **exits 0 and queues nothing** when the class limiter suppresses one (a `lifecycle` ping inside its 300 s window). `claude_ping.admits()` returns a REASON precisely so that *"we suppressed it"* and *"there was nothing to say"* stay distinguishable — folding that into `status: ok` would throw the distinction away at the last hop. The wrapper captures stdout, detects the `withheld:` marker, and records `status: withheld` with the limiter's reason.

Validation is duplicated at the workflow layer on purpose. `send_ping.py` already refuses `--kind` without `--why`, but it does so as a nonzero exit inside an SSH'd wrapper, surfacing as a generic "script returned nonzero" on a run page nobody opens. The outer check names the field. The script keeps its own guards because it is also reachable directly on the VM — two checks of one rule is the correct shape when only one of them is ever read.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — no schema, no order path. Three optional parameters on a Tier-1, non-mutating observability action.

## Test plan

- [x] **9 new tests** in `tests/test_send_ping_action_kind.py`, driving the real wrapper against a tmp `REPO_DIR` with a fake producer that records its argv — so the assertions are about what was *invoked*, not about log lines.
- [x] **Ran them.** `pytest` is absent from the sandbox, so each test function was executed directly through a minimal runner: **9/9 pass.** One failure on the first run was a wrong slice index in a test I had just written, not in the code; fixed by asserting the full argv instead.
- [x] **`tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py`: 29/29 pass** (run through a `pytest` shim). The 4 that first errored were the harness not applying the fixture's own bare-`on:` → `True` normalisation — my harness, not this change.
- [x] `canonical-doc-coherence` passes with the `docs/claude/system-actions.md` row updated.
- [x] `run_guards.py`: **PASS 41 · FAIL 3**, and all three failures are absent sandbox tooling — 2× `python3 -m pytest` (not installed) and `lint-imports` exit **127** (not installed). Tooling, not defects.
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] ⚠️ **Not yet exercised on the fleet.** Landing this does not by itself send a classed ping; the action must also reach the VM. Until then the three classes stay unreachable in production — which is the state this PR exists to end — and they will not be reported as tested until a real dispatch has fired each one.

⚠️ **This depends on #10674 for the RESULT to be meaningful, not in order to merge.** Without #10674 a classed ping still lands in the trader chat. This PR changes a ping's SHAPE and GATING; #10674 changes its DESTINATION. Independent changes to the same journey.
